contract.structural_score_basis: Ethereum crvUSD has no measured token-upgrade surface. Curve DAO controls arbitrary factory execution and ceiling increases. The 5-of-9 emergency Safe has restricted undelayed functions, including LLv2 policy/callback replacement and conditional oracle repair. The WETH policy adds YieldBasis DAO configuration and an upgradeable signed-price verifier whose ultimate owner governance remains unresolved. Structural 5.5 is retained from the historical assessment, pending explicit reassessment of expanded permissions; it is not newly endorsed by the November 2 review.
code_facts: At Ethereum block 26,327,058 (2026-11-02 12:20:23 UTC), ControllerFactory and the checked lending factories use LendingOwnerProxy 0xeda020b067872717901916a3b8c724c21f6080d1. Checked AMM factories use AmmOwnerProxy 0xeda0108d5bb8cde2ba4a59e22f3ed5d211c77187. Their immutable forwarding code is distinct from a token implementation-upgrade proxy.

Curve emergency Safe 0x467947ee34af926cf1dcac093870f613c96b1e0c remains 5-of-9. The lending proxy permits restricted LLv2 monetary-policy/callback replacement, zero-cap actions, deployment pauses and conditional oracle repair without a proxy-level delay. Oracle probes test availability/nonzero output, not economic correctness. Chainlink-path toggling works in both directions.

Only the DAO may execute arbitrary calls or increase issuance ceilings. Curve Ownership Voting retains its seven-day floor. DAO or current eDAO may revoke the proxy emergency address, but revocation neither undoes earlier actions nor removes the WETH policy emergency address.

The YieldBasis WETH/crvUSD policy is attached; deployed reserved-profit fraction is 43%, versus 42.2% in the forum specification. It controls pricing, fees and leveraged-token deposit checks, not direct crvUSD minting. YieldBasis DAO configures policy/verifier settings; its early-execution voting mode does not guarantee a seven-day update delay.

Curve emergency authority can kill and revive the WETH policy. Kill uses native pool fee/target behavior and refuses reports; it does not freeze prices. Curve policy replacement/removal requires the ordinary DAO execute route.

The signed-price verifier is upgradeable and trusted signers are owner-mutable. The ultimate governance threshold/delay behind its owner contract remains unresolved. An authenticated ETH report does not eliminate crvUSD peg risk; policy pricing treats crvUSD as one dollar.

Vote 1509 executed a further 30 million crvUSD mint/deposit for Resupply sreUSD, bringing operator mintLimit and mintedAmount to 60 million. Borrower debt, idle issuance and credit quality remain separate. The operator mint factory remains owned by the Curve Ownership Agent.

Current child-gauge bindings were checked on Arbitrum, Optimism, Sonic and Taiko with 5-of-9 emergency Safes sharing Ethereum owners. Optimism destination execution is verified; exact Arbitrum/Sonic/Taiko chronology remains unresolved. These are gauge controls, not a refreshed token-bridge audit.

The source/runtime review supports the checked proxy restrictions and policy attachment. A complete audit-to-deployment and bounty mapping for new privileged surfaces was not established. Historical audit branding is not coverage of every current authority path.

September token/bridge observations retain their original dates: Ethereum token upgrade absence; Arbitrum beacon/UpgradeExecutor exposure; Fraxtal bridge 3-of-5 authority; Optimism nested multisig threshold unresolved; BNB DVN internal signer membership unmeasured; Base local bridge gate measured but ultimate governance unresolved. These were not fully re-audited in November.
